reading: Thieves executed an elaborate heist, stealing 30,000 wine bottles worth €5m in Italy, according to media reports.
The incident at the Florence-based winery, Marchesi Antinori, is believed to be one of the largest heists of its kind in Italy.
Italian media further reported that 30,000 bottles of wine were collectively valued at approximately €5m (£4.2m) from the prestigious facility.
Marchesi Antinori, recognized as one of Italy's biggest family-owned wineries, stated the theft occurred at its storage facility in Tuscany on a Saturday.
This happened as the company was preparing to dispatch a substantial consignment to international customers abroad.
At least seven masked individuals reportedly deactivated the security alarms and disabled the cameras during the operation.
The perpetrators then utilized company forklifts to load two large trucks with the winery's prized Tignanello, Solaia, and Guado al Tasso Tuscan reds.
Renzo Cotarella, the chief executive, affirmed to Corriere della Sera that a theft of this magnitude and value was unprecedented in Italy.
He also expressed optimism that authorities would ultimately be able to trace the stolen merchandise.
Cotarella underscored this optimism by stating that 'Two trucks full of merchandise can't just disappear into thin air.'
He also suggested the specific selection of bottles, typically selling for between €150 and €500 each, implied the perpetrators were expert wine connoisseurs with potential insider knowledge.
The elaborate operation was only discovered on Monday morning when staff arrived on site, and no arrests have been made.
Established in 1385, Marchesi Antinori exports its products to 170 countries and recorded a revenue of €263 million (£223m) last year.
Italy has seen a surge in wine thefts this year, including recent incidents in the northern Piedmont region where hundreds of thousands of euros worth of bottles were taken.
